title: fix(floor): rank endpoints by expected billed cost with cache, and keep a shared prefix on one host
description:
# 🌙 dream: the openrouter floor ranks by sticker input rate and picks a host that never caches

- kind: reseed
- owner: ehmpathy/rhachet-brains-openrouter
- caught 2026-10-08

## .the cue that fired

at 5.1 i025 (`.behavior/v2026_09_20.review-cost-meter`, hash `30f4b366cf24fdfa37`) every review lane
on `openrouter/deepseek/flash` reported `cache.get: 0`. the lanes share large system-prompt heads
(two heads were byte-identical), and the repo already orders, primes, and pins for cache.

## .the gap, precisely

- **a real miss, not a gap in the report.** the adapter reads
  `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (`dist/infra/cast/asBrainSizeTokens.js`) and shows
  non-zero reads on other hosts (Morph 41,344, Decart 41,216). the billed `usage.cost` matches the
  full uncached rate to the cent:

  | run | in | out | in × $0.045/M + out × $1.2/M | billed |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `2026-10-08T03-59-13-202Z…` | 444,883 | 42,796 | $0.07138 | $0.071374935 |
  | `2026-10-08T03-59-13-563Z…` | 578,308 | 31,957 | $0.06437 | $0.064372260 |

- **every i024/i025 lane was served by Wafer** (`supply.provider: "Wafer"`, all ten runs on
  2026-10-08). openrouter's endpoint list for the model marks Wafer with
  `supports_implicit_caching: false`; only the first-party host marks `true`. Wafer's cache-read
  rate ($0.044/M) is ~2% under its prompt rate ($0.045/M), so even a hit would save almost naught
- **why Wafer every time:** `getAllQualifiedEndpoints.js` ranks with
  `getOneEndpointCostEstimate = tokens.input × pricePromptUsdPerToken`. the rank ignores the
  cache-read rate, whether the host caches at all, and the output rate — and output is most of
  each bill here ($0.051 of $0.071 on the first row)
- ⇒ **no local layout, prime, or warmer can make a host that never caches hit.** the floor's pick
  is the bound on the whole cache lever this route built

## .the scatter, measured — one slug, eight caches

the meter's `by provider` axis (`rhx review._.cost --of tree`), on this tree's corpus, 2026-10-14.
one brain slug, `openrouter/deepseek/flash`, landed on eight providers, and no provider cached
more than a tenth of what it was sent:

| provider | runs | prompt | cached |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wafer | 362 | 147.7M | 9.1% |
| Morph | 346 | 89.5M | 7.0% |
| Decart | 116 | 41.7M | 1.1% |
| InferenceNet | 72 | 30.5M | 1.2% |
| DigitalOcean | 22 | 8.7M | 0.7% |
| DeepInfra | 9 | 4.4M | 0.2% |
| Sail Research | 6 | 2.7M | 0.1% |

- the floor's second key is live `throughputTps`, and `speed=min50tps` filters on it too, so the
  qualified set and its order drift call by call. a prefix one call wrote on Wafer is read by the
  next on Morph, which never saw it
- a partitioned round at `5.3.verification i004` sent the prime and every partition to Wafer, with
  prompts byte-identical for 3,407 lines, and read 1,280 cache tokens of ~378k. so even one host
  holds no prefix across one round's calls, which is the affinity dream's half

## .the shape of the fix

1. rank qualified endpoints by EXPECTED billed cost, not sticker input rate:
   `uncached × prompt + cached × cache_read + est_output × completion`, where `cached` is the share
   of the ask the caller expects to repeat (its system prompt), and a host marked
   `supports_implicit_caching: false` counts `cache_read = prompt`
2. accept a caller hint for the expected output size (or a per-model default), since output often
   dominates
3. clamps: (a) `getAllQualifiedEndpoints` unit case — A (prompt $0.045, cache-read $0.044, no
   implicit cache) vs B (prompt $0.09, cache-read $0.009, implicit cache), a mostly-cached ask →
   B first; red today. (b) a cash case where breakdown parts sum to the billed total (see the peer
   dream `v2026_10_05.reseed.openrouter-cost-breakdown-is-a-rate-card-beside-a-billed-total`)
4. pairs with `v2026_10_06.reseed.openrouter-affinity-key-for-a-shared-prefix` (stick a prefix set to
   the host that served its prime) — the rank picks a host that caches, the affinity keeps the set
   on it

🟡 the upstream code note cites a decision to rank by input alone (its own `F20`). this overturns
that decision, so the upstream wisher must decide again with this evidence in hand.

## .why it is not done in this round

SAFE: yes. CLEAN: no — the rank lives in another repo's package; this repo can only consume the
corrected pick. the local half (the prime meet that never formed at i025) is repaired in this round.
